title: KV-conscious slice-lease negotiator with stochastic backoff
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Background: Continuous batching improves GPU utilization by aggregating many short requests into larger internal slices. However, aggressive batching can cause KV cache pressure and unpredictable preemption that violates tenant SLOs (p99 latency and tail throughput). This ticket implements a slice-lease negotiation protocol that is KV-aware and uses stochastic backoff to reduce hard preempts while preserving fairness across tenants and SLO tiers. The goal is to reduce SLO breaches for P0/P1 tenants while reclaiming GPU memory under high contention with graceful degradation for best-effort workloads.
proposal: We propose a lease-based admission/negotiation layer for continuous batches: each tenant slice acquires a time-limited lease on GPU slice resources and an associated KV residency token budget. When contention rises, the negotiator asks low-priority leases to 'shrink' (reduce token budget and max tokens of KV residency) instead of immediate hard preemptions. If tenants don't shrink voluntarily within a randomized backoff window, the negotiator issues a soft-yield that preserves progress (checkpoint/resume) and evicts non-critical KV segments. Key components: 1) Per-tenant SLO headroom estimator that converts latency gaps into a numeric urgency score. 2) KV-residency accounting on a per-lease basis (hotset score + estimated working set). 3) Stochastic backoff policy: low-priority leases receive randomized shrink windows proportional to their urgency rank to avoid synchronized evictions. 4) Memory-aware slice shrink: slices can reduce batch size or checkpoint KV to host local fast storage (NVMe) to free GPU memory. 5) Fairness ledger: long-term fairness enforced by maintaining a decaying credit balance per tenant; credits penalize repeated involuntary yields. 6) Canary rollout plan via runtime-1.22 with observability hooks for p99/p95 latency, kv-residency, preempt rate, and GPU memory defragmentation metrics.
acceptance_criteria: P0/P1 tenant p99 latency regression <= 5% compared to baseline under identical load in synthetic stress tests
Under 95th percentile KV pressure scenario, hard preemptions reduced by >= 60% vs current baseline
Average GPU memory reclaimed per incident >= 70% of target budget within 500ms without causing OOMs
Fairness: no tenant loses > 30% of its expected throughput for more than 3 consecutive cycles; decaying-credit ledger reflects enforcement actions
End-to-end integration tests and canary on dedicated pool for runtime-1.22 completed with monitoring dashboards and automated rollback triggers

notes: 2026-03-02: Spike showed that naive hard-preempt causes KV thrashing and increases p99 for high-priority tenants due to cold-KV misses.
2026-03-04: Prototype headroom estimator using EWMA of latency residuals; initial results correlate well with SLO breaks in synthetic trace.
2026-03-06: Decided to prefer shrink+checkpoint over immediate eviction for best-effort tenants to preserve throughput and avoid repeated cold misses.
2026-03-08: Memory-aware shrink requires changes to KV layout; will add a 'cold segment' marker to allow prioritized eviction without compaction pressure.
2026-03-10: Tradeoff: stochastic backoff reduces synchronization but adds variance to fairness; plan to compensate with decaying-credit ledger that enforces longer-term fairness windows.
2026-03-11: Eng review: runtime changes likely ~2% CPU overhead for accounting; acceptable for Dedicated pools but will gate behind config flags for Hosted initially.
